chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is performing Tamattu' and cannot find a sacrificial animal, let him fast three days during Hajj and seven when he returns to his family. If this eludes him and he has a stay after departing (from Mina), let him fast three days in Mecca. And if he does not have a stay, let him fast on the road or in his family. And if he has a stay in Mecca and wishes to fast the seven, he should leave fasting for the duration of his journey to his family or a month, then fast.'

key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for expiation if one cannot afford a sacrificial animal during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a Mu'tamir in Hajj al-Tamattu' who lacks the means for a sacrificial animal, prescribing ten days of fasting. It provides nuanced rulings for those who delay departure or wish to combine the fasting periods, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding ritual purity and obligation fulfillment. The text highlights the flexibility within Shia fiqh to accommodate travelers' circumstances while maintaining the spiritual integrity of the Hajj rites.
